abstract: This paper develops a novel measure of monetary shocks that accounts for the endogenous response of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) to higher moments of expected economic outcomes. First, I use quantile regression to estimate the conditional distribution of Federal Reserve forecasts and construct indicators of uncertainty and skewness. Second, I show that, unlike other measures proposed in the literature, these indicators have strong predictive power for the changes in the Federal funds rate deliberated by the FOMC. This suggests that point forecasts alone do not fully capture the FOMC’s systematic response to the economic outlook, with implications for the identification of monetary policy shocks. In particular, once higher moments are controlled for, the response of macroeconomic and financial variables is more closely aligned with theoretical predictions.
journal: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
title: Higher-Moments-Robust Monetary Policy Shocks

abstract: We examine whether upward mobility within a person’s reference group changes the subjective value of own and reference income. Standard relative-income models interpret higher peer income mainly as status loss. We argue that this view is incomplete. In mobile reference groups, higher peer income may also signal attainable opportunities, consistent with a “tunnel effect”; at the same time, mobility can raise aspirations and reduce satisfaction with one’s own income, creating what we call the “price of hope”. Using the Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP) for 2000–2020, we combine individual fixed effects with leave-one-out reference income and leave-one-out reference-group-year measures of realised upward income dynamics. Among individuals below their reference income, the negative association between reference income and life satisfaction is strong in low-mobility environments but largely attenuated when mobility is high. The own-income gradient is also smaller in high-mobility environments. These patterns are weaker among individuals at or above their reference income and robust across alternative mobility measures, reference-group definitions, median reference income, and controls for within-group inequality. Mobility, therefore, changes the meaning of income: it makes richer peers less costly as a status benchmark, but lowers the subjective return to current own income by shifting aspirations upward.
title: The price of hope: Reference-group mobility and the subjective value of income

abstract: Trust can attract fraud when it delays verification. We develop a two-market signaling model in which generative AI lowers fabrication, verification, and targeting costs. When fabrication becomes profitable before verification, claim credibility first falls and later recovers. Across markets, higher prior quality can delay verification, creating an interval in which only the lower-quality market checks. If targeting becomes profitable in this interval, deceptive sellers enter the higher-quality but less vigilant market, and their entry can initially reverse its reliability advantage. The inflow also triggers verification and deters further entry. We call this self-limiting mechanism trust arbitrage. In the age of generative AI, trust can thus create an endogenous but temporary protection gap that redirects deception across markets.
title: When trust attracts fraud: AI and trust arbitrage

abstract: We develop a dynamic model for digital service firms, which invest in monetization to generate revenues from services that customers may not fully pay for. A key novelty of our model is that customer acquisition by firms need not translate directly into the generation of revenues. Our model explains why such firms often build a large customer base and become highly valued while continuing to suffer losses, fueled by substantial upfront SG&A expenditures with sizable though risky growth potential. Counterfactual analysis reveals that hurdles to monetization—such as regulation aimed at protecting customer privacy—make firms smaller and less innovative, whereas direct revenues from customers support technological advancement.
title: The monetization of innovation

abstract: We propose a conceptual framework to study motivated beliefs in strategic settings. We consider static games in which players' utilities depend directly on their beliefs about others' actions. We introduce Optimal Belief Equilibrium (OBE), in which each player jointly chooses an action and a belief that justifies that action so as to maximize his belief-based utility given opponents' play. We characterize OBE through an auxiliary game and establish existence in finite games. As a leading case, we focus on anticipatory utility, where players value both realized and anticipated material payoffs. We analyze how equilibrium behavior varies with the intensity of anticipatory motives in several broad classes of games: coordination games, public-good contribution games, centipede games, and cheap talk. We show that optimistic beliefs about others' behavior can facilitate efficient coordination, encourage free-riding, sustain trust-based relationships, and make communication persuasive despite transparent conflicts of interest.
title: Optimal Belief Equilibrium

abstract: Property rights system reform is a crucial means to stimulate rural development vitality and facilitate the strategy of rural revitalization. However, there is still insufficient empirical evidence regarding whether property rights delineation can reduce farming households’ precautionary savings and thereby boost their consumption. To address this, this study takes China’s new round of rural land rights confirmation (RLRC) as an example. It constructs a quasi-natural experiment based on data from the 2013 and 2015 China Household Finance Survey (CHFS) and the 2018 China Labor-force Dynamics Survey (CLDS). By comprehensively employing the Difference-in-Differences (DID) method, the Instrumental variable (IV) method, and the Mediation effect model, this study empirically investigates the causal relationship between RLRC and farming households’ consumption, with a particular focus on the mediating effect of precautionary savings. This study finds that the RLRC promotes the growth of farming households’ consumption, and this conclusion remains valid after undergoing various robustness tests. Mechanism analysis reveals that RLRC boosts farming households’ consumption by reducing their precautionary savings, and this mechanism remains robust and effective even after the implementation of the “separation of three rights” reform of rural land and the pilot programs for the mortgage loans of rural land management rights. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that for households with younger household heads and those possessing richer human capital and social capital, the stimulating effect of RLRC on their consumption is more pronounced. Further analysis shows that RLRC primarily promotes subsistence consumption among farming households, rather than developmental consumption, while also having a positive effect on their income improvement. This study not only provides a new explanation for the paradoxical phenomenon of “farming households having money but being reluctant to spend it” but also offers new empirical evidence for government departments to optimize or formulate consumption stimulation policies.

title: Can property rights delineation incentivize farming households’ consumption? An analysis from the perspective of precautionary savings

abstract: Public debates on genetically modified (GM) crops center on environmental and health risks, yet evidence remains limited and focuses largely on herbicide-tolerant varieties or on local exposure, leaving the broad consequences of insect-resistant crops unclear. Insect-resistant crops can reduce pesticide use and generate health effects beyond directly exposed farmers. Yet their net effects are ambiguous, as any environmental gains may be offset by crop substitution, pest resistance, industrial expansion, and land-use change. We exploit the staggered approval of Bt cotton across China, combined with river networks that link cotton-growing areas to downstream residents. Bt cotton approval leads to significant downstream reductions in under-five mortality by 4.2%, driven by reduced pesticide use and improved water quality. In aggregate, Bt cotton approval reduces national pesticide use by 3.2%. The findings show that the social value of insect-resistant GM crops can be significantly underestimated, as they generate positive health externalities through environmental spillovers.

title: The health effects of genetically modified crops

abstract: The rise in net dollar bond positions of non-US investors has increased the net hedging demand for dollar short positions. We show how high variability of hedging and a negative demand elasticity for dollar short positions can explain increased FX volatility and the strong negative correlation between changes in net hedging and dollar spot rate returns, which reaches up to −70% for the dollar currency return index in 2012–2022. We also construct granular instruments based on idiosyncratic bank capital measures which identify the hedging demand elasticity as negative, suggesting that less hedging is demanded if the dollar appreciates.
title: Can time-varying currency risk hedging explain exchange rates?

abstract: Concerns about offspring’s life quality are often cited as a motivation for caring about climate change. This paper investigates the hypothesized causal effect of grandparenthood on climate change worries, using panel data surveys among British families. Specifically, we study whether becoming a grandparent increases these worries. We employ two different study designs to deal with endogeneity of grandparenthood. Across designs, the assumptions required to identify causal effects differ and are non-nested but give a remarkably congruent result: We find no empirical support for a relationship between grandparental status and concerns about climate change.
title: For the future of our grandchildren: Grandparenthood and climate change concerns

abstract: This study examines how Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) payment intensity and national governance quality jointly shape technical efficiency in agricultural land use. The sample covers the 27 EU member states over 2005–2022, giving 486 balanced observations. We estimate a per-hectare panel stochastic frontier model. Per-hectare normalisation lowers the maximum variance inflation factor from 14.98 to 3.25. CAP payment intensity is the inverse hyperbolic sine of the implicit subsidy per hectare of utilised agricultural area (UAA). This measure correlates with directly reported product subsidies at r = 0.9994. The governance interaction is the central result. The CAP × WGI term is positive and significant across pooled, event-study, Mundlak, control-function, and no-dummy specifications (δ₃ between +0.008 and +0.018, p < 0.001 in five of six specifications). The stand-alone CAP effect weakens when subsidies are removed from the dependent variable, so we report it as secondary. A latent class model identifies two production technologies. Capital elasticity is positive in both classes, which resolves the negative aggregate capital coefficient. Efficiency rankings shift across specifications (Spearman ρ ≈ 0.4 between pooled and panel estimates), so we treat country rankings as indicative. The marginal CAP effect on inefficiency changes sign near a governance z-score of about 0.87. We interpret all results as conditional associations. They support governance-aware targeting of CAP payments rather than a prescriptive redesign.
abstract_zh: 本研究考察共同农业政策（CAP）支付强度与国家治理质量如何共同塑造农业土地利用的技术效率。样本涵盖2005—2022年27个欧盟成员国，共486个平衡观测值。我们估计了一个每公顷面板随机前沿模型。每公顷归一化使最大方差膨胀因子从14.98降至3.25。CAP支付强度为已利用农业面积（UAA）每公顷隐性补贴的反双曲正弦。该测度与直接报告的产品补贴相关系数为r = 0.9994。治理交互项是核心结果。CAP × WGI项在混合、事件研究、Mundlak、控制函数和无虚拟变量设定中均为正且显著（δ₃介于+0.008至+0.018之间，六种设定中有五种p < 0.001）。当从因变量中移除补贴后，CAP的独立效应减弱，因此我们将其作为次要结果报告。潜在类别模型识别出两种生产技术。资本弹性在两个类别中均为正，这解决了总体资本系数为负的问题。效率排名在不同设定间发生变动（混合估计与面板估计之间的Spearman ρ ≈ 0.4），因此我们将国家排名视为指示性的。CAP对无效率的边际效应在治理z分数约为0.87附近改变符号。我们将所有结果解释为条件关联。这些结果支持对CAP支付进行治理意识的目标定位，而非规范性重新设计。
title: CAP regime shifts, institutional quality, and technical efficiency in agricultural land use across the EU: A panel stochastic frontier analysis
title_zh: 欧盟共同农业政策制度变迁、制度质量与农业土地利用技术效率：基于面板随机前沿分析

abstract: This study proposes an inverted U-shaped relationship between ancestral state experience and democratic preferences. Compared to stateless societies, primitive states are likely to foster proto-democratic values through a nascent balance between central authority and local autonomy. In contrast, more consolidated pre-modern states typically entrench authoritarian regimes, thereby undermining norms of participatory individual engagement. Evidence aligns with this hypothesis. Using data from the Ethnographic Atlas, we show that moderate exposure to ancestral statehood is positively associated with democratic preferences, while excessive exposure has the reverse pattern. Survey-based evidence corroborates this pattern, suggesting the intergenerational transmission of the ancestral legacy on democratic orientations.
abstract_zh: 本研究提出祖先国家经验与民主偏好之间存在倒U型关系。与无国家社会相比，原始国家可能通过中央权威与地方自治之间初生的平衡来培育原初民主价值观。相比之下，更为巩固的前现代国家通常强化威权政体，从而削弱参与性个体投入的规范。证据与这一假说相符。利用《民族志图集》的数据，我们表明，对祖先国家形态的中等程度接触与民主偏好正相关，而过度接触则呈现相反模式。基于调查的证据印证了这一模式，表明祖先遗产对民主取向具有代际传递效应。
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
source_issue: Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization, Volume 250
title: Ancestral origins of democratic preferences: The role of state experience
title_zh: 民主偏好的祖先起源：国家经验的作用

abstract: This paper studies the influence of corporate contributions on political selection and electoral outcomes. To identify the effects, I analyze a Brazilian reform that banned firms’ contributions using a weighted difference-in-differences strategy, exploiting variation in candidates’ reliance on corporate funding prior to the reform. I find that the ban fosters political competition by encouraging challengers and new candidates to run for office. Instead, the reform penalizes incumbents funded by firms by decreasing their likelihood of re-election. These adverse effects are particularly pronounced among underperforming incumbents. I also show that firms tend to donate more to mayors associated with higher corruption, a pattern that does not emerge for other donor types.
abstract_zh: 本文研究企业捐款对政治选拔和选举结果的影响。为识别其效应，我分析了一项禁止企业捐款的巴西改革，采用加权双重差分策略，并利用改革前候选人对企业资金依赖程度的差异。我发现，该禁令通过鼓励挑战者和新候选人竞选公职，促进了政治竞争。相反，该改革惩罚了由企业资助的现任者，降低了其连任的可能性。这些不利效应在表现不佳的现任者中尤为明显。我还表明，企业往往向与更高腐败程度相关的市长捐赠更多，而这一模式在其他捐赠者类型中并未出现。
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
source_issue: Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization, Volume 250
title: Corporate contributions and political selection: Evidence from Brazil
title_zh: 企业贡献与政治选拔：来自巴西的证据

abstract: Modern manufacturing often requires firms to share confidential information with outside suppliers, some of whom also supply their competitors. Using more than 160,000 contracts from the global automotive industry, this column examines how manufacturers respond to this risk and the costs of doing so. The findings suggest that when legal protection is weak, firms may instead turn to contractual exclusivity by limiting the number of manufacturers their suppliers can serve, reducing the suppliers’ customer base and bargaining power and potentially weakening their incentives to invest. Stronger legal protection reduces the need for this contractual response and can therefore support broader supplier networks.
abstract_zh: 现代制造业往往要求企业与外部供应商共享机密信息，而其中一些供应商同时也为竞争对手供货。本文利用全球汽车行业超过16万份合同，考察制造商如何应对这一风险以及由此产生的成本。研究结果表明，当法律保护薄弱时，企业可能转而借助合同排他性，通过限制供应商所能服务的制造商数量，削弱供应商的客户基础与议价能力，并可能削弱其投资激励。更强的法律保护会降低对这种合同性应对措施的需求，从而能够支撑更广泛的供应商网络。
authors: David Angenendt, Giacomo Calzolari, Alireza Naghavi
title: Spilling secrets and shrinking chains: How weak laws narrow supply networks
title_zh: 泄露秘密与收缩链条：弱法律如何缩小供应网络

abstract: Local labor market shocks are difficult to insure against. Using confidential micro data from the U.S. Census Bureau’s Longitudinal Business Database, we document that firms redistribute the adverse employment impacts of local demand shocks across regions through their internal networks of establishments. We find large elasticities of non-tradable establishment-level employment with respect to house prices in other counties in which the firm has establishments. Consistent with theory, these elasticities increase with the extent of firms’ financial constraints. Further, and consistent with the notion that firms smooth out the impacts of local demand shocks across regions, we find that establishments of firms with more expansive regional networks exhibit lower elasticities with respect to house prices in the establishment’s own county. To account for general equilibrium adjustments, we also consider total non-tradable employment at the county level. Similar to what we found at the establishment level, we find that non-tradable county-level employment responds strongly to local demand shocks in other counties linked through firms’ internal networks of establishments. These results are not driven by direct demand spillovers from nearby counties, common county-level shocks to house prices, or local demand shocks affecting non-tradable employment in distant counties indirectly through the trade channel. Overall, our results suggest that firms play an important role in the extent to which local labor market risks are shared across regions.
title: Redistribution of Local Demand Shocks through Firms' Internal Networks
title_zh: 地方需求冲击通过企业内部网络再分配

abstract: this paper we study the relevance and mechanics of consumption network effects. We use long panel data on the entire Danish population to construct a measure of consumption based on administrative tax records, and define the peer groups in terms of workplace, occupation, education, and age. We then apply an IV strategy, and fixed effect models, to recover the effects. Our instruments arise naturally from the network structure and firms shocks. The estimated effects are statistically significant and relevant for policies as they generate non- negligible multiplier effect. Further, the results are consistent with a Keeping-upmodel.
abstract_zh: 本文研究消费网络效应的相关性及其机制。我们使用丹麦全体人口的长期面板数据，基于行政税务记录构建消费衡量指标，并从工作场所、职业、教育和年龄等方面界定同伴群体。随后，我们运用工具变量策略和固定效应模型来识别这些效应。我们的工具变量自然来源于网络结构与企业冲击。估计出的效应在统计上显著，并且对政策具有相关性，因为它们产生了不可忽视的乘数效应。此外，结果与“攀比”模型相一致。
title: Consumption Network Effects

abstract: This paper first develops a simple model to clarify the links between leisure time use and skill formation. It then explores empirically how youths allocate their time. We focus on sports as a popular activity and estimate its effect on behavioral and economic outcomes. We exploit data from the German Socio-Economic Panel that offers the unique advantage of both a large, representative sample and high quality behavioral measures. We employ a flexible strategy combining propensity score matching and regression to account for self selection. Our results suggest that structured leisure activities like sports contribute to the development of nonacademic skills.
abstract_zh: 本文首先构建一个简单模型，以厘清休闲时间使用与技能形成之间的联系。随后，本文从实证角度探讨青少年如何分配其时间。我们聚焦于体育运动这一广受欢迎的活动，并估计其对行为与经济结果的影响。我们利用德国社会经济面板数据，该数据具有既提供大规模代表性样本又具备高质量行为测量指标的独特优势。我们采用一种灵活策略，将倾向得分匹配与回归相结合，以处理自选择问题。我们的结果表明，诸如体育运动这类有组织的休闲活动有助于非学术性技能的发展。
title: Quality Leisure Time and Youth Development
title_zh: 优质休闲时间与青年发展

abstract: Macroeconomic models often incorporate some form of wage stickiness to help account for employment fluctuations. However, a recent literature calls into question this approach, citing evidence of new hire wage cyclicality from panel data studies as evidence for contractual wage flexibility for new hires, which is the relevant margin for employment volatility. We analyze data from the SIPP and find that the wages for new hires coming from unemployment are no more cyclical than those of existing workers, suggesting wages are sticky at the relevant margin. The new hire wage cyclicality found in earlier studies instead appears to reflect cyclical average wage gains of workers making job-to-job transitions, which we interpret as evidence of procyclical match quality for new hires from employment. We then develop a quantitative general equilibrium model with sticky wages via staggered contracting, on-the-job search, and variable match quality, and show that it can account for both the panel data evidence and aggregate labor market regularities. An additional implication of the model is that a sullying effect of recessions emerges, along the lines originally suggested by Barlevy (2002).
title: Unemployment Fluctuations, Match Quality, and the Wage Cyclicality of New Hires
title_zh: 失业波动、匹配质量与新雇员工资的周期性

abstract: Are some management practices akin to a technology that can explain company and national productivity, or do they simply reflect contingent management styles? We collect data on core management practices from over 11,000 firms in 34 countries. We find large cross-country differences in the adoption of basic management practices, with the US having the highest size-weighted average management score. We present a formal model of "Management as a Technology", and structurally estimate it using panel data to recover parameters including the depreciation rate and adjustment costs of managerial capital (both found to be larger than for tangible non-managerial capital). Our model also predicts (i) a positive effect of management on firm performance; (ii) a positive relationship between product market competition and average management quality (part of which stems from the larger covariance between management with firm size as competition strengthens); and (iii) a rise (fall) in the level (dispersion) of management with firm age. We find strong empirical support for all of these predictions in our data. Finally, building on our model, we find that differences in management practices account for about 30% of cross-country total factor productivity differences.
title: Management as a Technology

abstract: This paper examines the role of international trade for job polarization, where mid-wage occupations decline while employment opportunities of workers in both high- and low-wage occupations increase. With employer-employee matched data on virtually all workers and firms in Denmark between 1999 and 2009, we use instrumental-variables techniques and a quasi-natural trade liberalization experiment to show that import competition has been a significant cause of job polarization. Comparing import competition to other explanations of job polarization, import competition is quantitatively comparable to technical change as the most important alternative explanation of the hollowing out of middle-class jobs, and only import competition explains also the increase in employment opportunities in the high- and low-wage tails. Worker movement from exposed middle-class jobs up into high-wage or down into low-wage jobs is shaped by worker education and skill, and especially by task characteristics of the worker’s occupation. We find that manual tasks are central for the impact of trade because foreign workers compete against domestic workers, in contrast to technical progress which pits man versus machine.
abstract_zh: 本文考察国际贸易在就业极化中的作用，即中等工资职业萎缩，而高工资和低工资职业劳动者的就业机会增加。基于1999年至2009年间丹麦几乎所有劳动者和企业的雇主—雇员匹配数据，我们运用工具变量技术和一项准自然贸易自由化实验表明，进口竞争是就业极化的重要成因。将进口竞争与就业极化的其他解释进行比较，进口竞争在数量上与技术变革相当，同为中产阶级就业空心化的最重要替代解释，且只有进口竞争还能解释高工资和低工资两端就业机会的增加。劳动者从受冲击的中产阶级岗位向上流入高工资岗位或向下流入低工资岗位，受劳动者教育和技能、尤其是其职业任务特征的塑造。我们发现，手工任务对贸易的影响至关重要，因为外国劳动者与本国劳动者竞争，这与技术进步形成对比，后者是人与机器的竞争。
title: International Trade and Job Polarization: Evidence at the Worker-Level
title_zh: 国际贸易与就业极化：劳动者层面的证据

abstract: In a market in which sellers compete for heterogeneous buyers by posting mechanisms, we analyze how the properties of the meeting technology affect the allocation of buyers to sellers. We show that a separate submarket for each type of buyer is the efficient outcome if and only if meetings are bilateral. In contrast, a single market with all agents is optimal if and only if the meeting technology satisfies a novel condition, which we call “joint concavity.” Both outcomes can be decentralized by sellers posting auctions combined with a fee that is paid by (or to) all buyers with whom the seller meets. Finally, we compare joint concavity to two other properties of meeting technologies, invariance and non rivalry, and explain the differences.
title: Search Frictions, Competing Mechanisms and Optimal Market Segmentation
title_zh: 搜索摩擦、竞争机制与最优市场细分
